description: Liumi Deep Space is an aerospace software initiative led by solo architect Muhammad Hasnain Sabqi. We engineered ADMOS: a zero-cloud medical cockpit for Mars missions. Powered by Liumi VectorCore's 0.061ms SIMD INT8 engine, it fuses biosignals, voice biomarkers, and audited NASA-STD-3001 emergency protocols to protect astronauts during communication blackouts. From native C-ABI retrieval to the 60 FPS cockpit HUD, the entire avionics suite was engineered, tested, and audited in-house.
summary:
During deep-space transit to Mars, radio signals take up to 22 minutes to reach Earth, creating a 44-minute round-trip blackout. When acute life-support emergencies happen during spacewalks, astronauts cannot wait for Mission Control, and cloud-based AI is impossible.

ADMOS (Autonomous Deep-Space Medical Operations System) is an edge-native, zero-cloud medical cockpit that keeps astronauts alive autonomously. It ingests multi-sensor biomedical telemetry, filters microgravity workout artifacts using Wavelet Signal Quality Indexing (SQI), and passively extracts 64-dimensional acoustic voice biomarkers to detect hypoxic speech before physical collapse.

When a crisis occurs, ADMOS queries official NASA-STD-3001 and Exploration Medical Capabilities (ExMC) emergency checklists using Liumi VectorCore—a zero-copy, SIMD INT8 native C-ABI vector engine—retrieving actionable survival protocols in just 0.061 milliseconds. ADMOS replaces 500-page paper flight manuals with instant, deterministic edge intelligence.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

ADMOS is an autonomous medical cockpit engine engineered for deep-space missions beyond Low Earth Orbit. Operating under strict compute and zero-connectivity constraints, ADMOS functions across three integrated layers:

1. Telemetry Ingestion & Signal Quality Indexing (SQI): Continuous biosignal streams (ECG, PPG, SpO2, respiration, and cabin CO2) undergo real-time noise rejection using Welch power spectral density (5–15 Hz QRS band) and skewness analysis, eliminating false alarms caused by microgravity exercise.

2. Passive Acoustic Biomarker Engine: A 64-dimensional feature extraction pipeline (MFCCs, spectral contrast, and pitch tracking) evaluates comms audio to detect vocal tract motor degradation (hypoxia, cognitive overload, and panic) before an astronaut loses consciousness.

3. Sub-Millisecond NASA Protocol Retrieval: Rather than requiring astronauts to flip through 500-page Flight Data File manuals during emergencies, ADMOS embeds symptom vectors and executes a sub-0.1ms SIMD INT8 search using Liumi VectorCore (.lvc). It instantly matches conditions against official NASA-STD-3001 and ExMC checklists.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Closes NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Exploration Medical Capabilities Gaps Med01 and Med07 (autonomous diagnosis and treatment during comms blackout).

- Zero-Click Medical Guidance: Emergency checklists appear on the cockpit HUD within 0.061 milliseconds without requiring crew search.

- Flight-Avionics Viable: Operates with deterministic execution, zero heap thrashing, and no cloud dependencies, making it viable for radiation-hardened flight hardware.

Tools, Languages, & Hardware:

- Backend: Python 3.11/3.12, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Librosa.

- Vector Engine: Liumi VectorCore (native x86_64 SIMD INT8 C-ABI integration).

- Cockpit HUD: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide-React, JetBrains Mono (offline bundled).

- Architecture: 20 Hz WebSocket streaming, 60 FPS Retina-scaled Canvas ECG renderer.

Creativity & Spaceflight Considerations:

Most biomedical solutions rely on cloud APIs or heavy deep learning models that crash on spaceflight hardware. ADMOS innovates by pairing mathematical digital signal processing with a zero-copy, SIMD INT8 vector search engine. This allows high-dimensional semantic matching of NASA medical standards directly on-device in under 70 microseconds.
